metadata.title: Odd or Even
metadata.description: Return a boolean stating whether n is even, correctly handling negative values.

instructions.main: Define `is_even(n)` returning `True` when `n` is even and `False` when it is odd — negative numbers included.
steps: Use `n % 2 == 0` — Python's `%` works for negatives too (`-4 % 2` is `0`).
Return a real boolean (`True`/`False`), not a string.
The program must leave the result of `is_even(-3)` in a variable named `result`.

hints.message: Define `def is_even(n):` and `return n % 2 == 0` — the `%` check works for negatives too.
Don't guard with `n > 0` — Python's `%` already handles negatives (`-4 % 2` is `0`), so one check covers every value.
Return a real boolean (`True`/`False`), not the strings `"True"`/`"False"`.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: `is_even` returns a proper boolean for negative values too.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Leave `result = is_even(-3)` at the end — for -3 it must be the boolean `False`.
